# the contributor audit: actual max sharing, physical interpolation, and tilt selection

## Arbitrary-base upward max propagation

PASS after the explicit deficient-rank repair in
`candidate 23587fb4045280b8`.
The generic-height assignment is acyclic, the worst-partner supremum
preserves continuity and convexity, and its maximum-sharing update
imposes every extreme anchored relation. Decomposing coefficient vectors
and retaining the same input points proves every remaining relation.
The exact hull has the prescribed fibers. Source credit correctly uses
the prescribed seed cost, not the larger final cost. The exponential
product calibration sums to 2^(m+1)-1 and is not a universal lower bound.
Max closure holds even for independently compatible arrays by actual
intersection; the signed shared-minimum correction is essential.

## Two-witness max sharing and its nonmonotonicity

PASS for `candidate 709f4ee1b13a1688`.
The piecewise linear radius sequences are concave, hence define actual
convex bodies. The selected slope-one critical covers have exact masses
3-10e and 3-11e; reflection of the outer interval into the opposite
inner one gives the matching all-direction lower bounds. The normalized
comparison has numerator -4e(1-4e). The alternative slope-one-half menu
is genuinely critical at zero but has first payment -1 on the max path.
The shared minimum's signed cost explains the opposite menu responses.

The added three-fiber example likewise has exact endpoint-isolating
upper bounds and reflected-pair lower bounds: separately descending
arrays can have a centrally symmetric maximum with unchanged true depth.
Thus no universal payment monotonicity under max is inferred.
the contributor reran the verifier: 112 exact checks PASS.

## Physical Minkowski interpolation

PASS for `candidate d9792f1ce8a8f405`.
Anchored compatibility distributes through Minkowski interpolation
exactly. On the square, minimizing the two affine top losses over
x_1+x_2=2x gives |x|, with the minimum attained by the displayed endpoints.
All vertical section bottoms remain -1, so this is an exact body identity.
The half-cap losses are 1/2 and 3/2 in the two branches, versus 1/2
in the interpolated body. Adding the binary-base rectangle of area8/3
gives true beta=3/10 and exact critical/slack covers. Averaged response
payment +1/10 and actual interpolation payment -1/10 are both correct.
The separate average-profile rectangle is acknowledged as a different
actual path, so the obstruction does not overclaim failure of all
possible response-cone closure.

The uniform-continuous-support-velocity sufficient condition for linear
TOTAL volume loss follows from mixed-volume telescoping and weak
continuity. Its missing hypothesis in the example is explicitly shown.
It is not promoted to a fixed-cap linearity theorem.

## Same-normal integer-tilt selection

PASS for `candidate 714bee9248df3ce6`,
with its stated ordinary paired-tail dependency for the final all-normal
global-criticality assertion. Minimum-norm clipping gives bounded tilt
representatives, while actual rays saturate in finite time and are not
coercive. The proper/full/empty one-sided derivatives have the correct
signs; their no-descent condition is inclusion of the ENTIRE negative
full-support zonotope, rather than existence of one allocation.

In the support-free rank-deficient case, a direction annihilating all
proper base vectors moves only saturated fibers until a first transition.
In full rank, positive proper section areas give a genuine anchored
relation, but not a whole-fiber contact equality. The one-sided density
derivatives in the second variation use the threshold's actual direction.

The centered simplex calculations are exact: cap (d-c)^d/d!, section
(d-c)^(d-1)/(d-1)!, Hessian2d^(d-2)/(d-2)!. Every nonzero canonical tilt
increases the cap mass, including saturation tails since2Gamma_d<1.
Thus forcing all minimizing tilts to a support transition is rigorously
blocked even by a truly critical product example. It does not block
changes of continuous normal, chosen source, or body deformation.
